U.note: True isometric 3D voxel world on a 32x32 grid with stacked heights, nine block types, place/erase, undo, hover ghost, starter terrain and saving; reads as a real block game, though the canvas is small on phones.

V.note: Flat 2D painter with eight colours and PNG save, but it starts empty, has no stacking, and its mobile grid lines are uneven.

W.note: Clean and well labelled with a counter, undo and keyboard picks, but it is just four block types painted flat on a blank grid with no depth, and the first screen shows nothing built.

X.note: Flat div grid with nine types and a side panel, but it is dark and empty with faint cells, and the mobile layout pushes the palette below the board.

Y.note: Minecraft-like side-view 32x32 world with textured blocks, sky, a tree and water, plus erase, undo and reset; it works well, though it is a 2D slice rather than a full world.

Z.note: Top-down grid with stackable columns up to height 6, a clear-armed flow and good keyboard support, but only three block types and a subtle pseudo-height look; the mobile toolbar clips.
